kjv.15:26: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, [even] the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
kjv.15:27: And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
kjv.16:1: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended.
kjv.16:2: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
kjv.16:3: And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.
kjv.16:4: But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you.
kjv.16:5: But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
kjv.16:6: But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.
kjv.16:7: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
kjv.16:8: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
kjv.16:9: Of sin, because they believe not on me;
kjv.16:10: Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
kjv.16:11: Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.
kjv.16:12: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
kjv.16:13: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, [that] shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
kjv.16:14: He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew [it] unto you.
kjv.16:15: All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall shew [it] unto you.
kjv.16:16: A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me, because I go to the Father.
kjv.16:17: Then said [some] of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?
kjv.16:18: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? we cannot tell what he saith.
kjv.16:19: Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, and said unto them, Do ye enquire among yourselves of that I said, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me?
kjv.16:20: Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
kjv.16:21: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world.
kjv.16:22: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
kjv.16:23: And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give [it] you.
kjv.16:24: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.
kjv.16:25: These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.
kjv.16:26: At that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you:
kjv.16:27: For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came out from God.
kjv.16:28: I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.
kjv.16:29: His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb.
kjv.16:30: Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.
kjv.16:31: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?
kjv.16:32: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
kjv.16:33: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
kjv.17:1: These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:
kjv.17:2: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him.
kjv.17:3: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
kjv.17:4: I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
kjv.17:5: And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
kjv.17:6: I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word.
kjv.17:7: Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee.
kjv.17:8: For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received [them], and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me.
kjv.17:9: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.
kjv.17:10: And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them.
kjv.17:11: And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we [are].
kjv.17:12: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.
kjv.17:13: And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
kjv.17:14: I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
kjv.17:15: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.
kjv.17:16: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
kjv.17:17: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
kjv.17:18: As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.
kjv.17:19: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.
kjv.17:20: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word;
kjv.17:21: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, [art] in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
kjv.17:22: And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one:
kjv.17:23: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.
kjv.17:24: Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
kjv.17:25: O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.
kjv.17:26: And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare [it]: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them.
kjv.18:1: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples.
kjv.18:2: And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus ofttimes resorted thither with his disciples.
kjv.18:3: Judas then, having received a band [of men] and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.
kjv.18:4: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye?
kjv.18:5: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am [he]. And Judas also, which betrayed him, stood with them.
kjv.18:6: As soon then as he had said unto them, I am [he], they went backward, and fell to the ground.
kjv.18:7: Then asked he them again, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.
kjv.18:8: Jesus answered, I have told you that I am [he]: if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:
kjv.18:9: That the saying might be fulfilled, which he spake, Of them which thou gavest me have I lost none.
kjv.18:10: Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest's servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
kjv.18:11: Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?
kjv.18:12: Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him,
kjv.18:13: And led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the high priest that same year.
kjv.18:14: Now Caiaphas was he, which gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
kjv.18:15: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and [so did] another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.
kjv.18:16: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
kjv.18:17: Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also [one] of this man's disciples? He saith, I am not.
kjv.18:18: And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.
kjv.18:19: The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine.
kjv.18:20: Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.
kjv.18:21: Why askest thou me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said.
kjv.18:22: And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?
kjv.18:23: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?
kjv.18:24: Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.
kjv.18:25: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also [one] of his disciples? He denied [it], and said, I am not.
kjv.18:26: One of the servants of the high priest, being [his] kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
kjv.18:27: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.
kjv.18:28: Then led they Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover.
kjv.18:29: Pilate then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring ye against this man?
kjv.18:30: They answered and said unto him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up unto thee.
kjv.18:31: Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:
kjv.18:32: That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying what death he should die.
kjv.18:33: Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?
kjv.18:34: Jesus answered him, Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of me?
kjv.18:35: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?
kjv.18:36: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.
kjv.18:37: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.
kjv.18:38: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault [at all].
kjv.18:39: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
kjv.18:40: Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
kjv.19:1: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged [him].
kjv.19:2: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put [it] on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,
kjv.19:3: And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.
kjv.19:4: Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.
kjv.19:5: Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And [Pilate] saith unto them, Behold the man!
kjv.19:6: When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify [him], crucify [him]. Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify [him]: for I find no fault in him.
kjv.19:7: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.
kjv.19:8: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid;
kjv.19:9: And went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.
kjv.19:10: Then saith Pilate unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to crucify thee, and have power to release thee?
kjv.19:11: Jesus answered, Thou couldest have no power [at all] against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath the greater sin.
kjv.19:12: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar's friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
kjv.19:13: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.
kjv.19:14: And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!
kjv.19:15: But they cried out, Away with [him], away with [him], crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.
kjv.19:16: Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led [him] away.
kjv.19:17: And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called [the place] of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha:
kjv.19:18: Where they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.
kjv.19:19: And Pilate wrote a title, and put [it] on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.
kjv.19:20: This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, [and] Greek, [and] Latin.
kjv.19:21: Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.
kjv.19:22: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.
kjv.19:23: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also [his] coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.
kjv.19:24: They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.
kjv.19:25: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the [wife] of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
kjv.19:26: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!
kjv.19:27: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own [home].
kjv.19:28: After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst.
kjv.19:29: Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a spunge with vinegar, and put [it] upon hyssop, and put [it] to his mouth.
kjv.19:30: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
kjv.19:31: The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and [that] they might be taken away.
kjv.19:32: Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him.
kjv.19:33: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:
kjv.19:34: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.
kjv.19:35: And he that saw [it] bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe.
kjv.19:36: For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
kjv.19:37: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.
kjv.19:38: And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave [him] leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.
kjv.19:39: And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound [weight].
kjv.19:40: Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.
kjv.19:41: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.
kjv.19:42: There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews' preparation [day]; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.
kjv.20:1: The first [day] of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.
kjv.20:2: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.
kjv.20:3: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.
kjv.20:4: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
kjv.20:5: And he stooping down, [and looking in], saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.
kjv.20:6: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,
kjv.20:7: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.
kjv.20:8: Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.
kjv.20:9: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
kjv.20:10: Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.
kjv.20:11: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, [and looked] into the sepulchre,
kjv.20:12: And seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
kjv.20:13: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.
kjv.20:14: And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.
kjv.20:15: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
kjv.20:16: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.
kjv.20:17: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and [to] my God, and your God.
kjv.20:18: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and [that] he had spoken these things unto her.
kjv.20:19: Then the same day at evening, being the first [day] of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace [be] unto you.
kjv.20:20: And when he had so said, he shewed unto them [his] hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord.
kjv.20:21: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace [be] unto you: as [my] Father hath sent me, even so send I you.
kjv.20:22: And when he had said this, he breathed on [them], and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:
kjv.20:23: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; [and] whose soever [sins] ye retain, they are retained.
kjv.20:24: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
kjv.20:25: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.
kjv.20:26: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: [then] came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace [be] unto you.
kjv.20:27: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust [it] into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
kjv.20:28: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
kjv.20:29: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed [are] they that have not seen, and [yet] have believed.
kjv.20:30: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book:
kjv.20:31: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
kjv.21:1: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he [himself].
kjv.21:2: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
kjv.21:3: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
kjv.21:4: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
kjv.21:5: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.
kjv.21:6: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
kjv.21:7: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt [his] fisher's coat [unto him], (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea.
kjv.21:8: And the other disciples came in a little ship; (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits,) dragging the net with fishes.
kjv.21:9: As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
kjv.21:10: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.
kjv.21:11: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
kjv.21:12: Jesus saith unto them, Come [and] dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
kjv.21:13: Jesus then cometh, and taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish likewise.
kjv.21:14: This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.
kjv.21:15: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, [son] of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
kjv.21:16: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, [son] of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
kjv.21:17: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, [son] of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
kjv.21:18: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry [thee] whither thou wouldest not.
kjv.21:19: This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
kjv.21:20: Then Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee?
kjv.21:21: Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what [shall] this man [do]?
kjv.21:22: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee? follow thou me.
kjv.21:23: Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee?
kjv.21:24: This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.
kjv.21:25: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.

bsb.1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
bsb.1:2: He was with God in the beginning.
bsb.1:3: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.
bsb.1:4: In Him was life, and that life was the light of men.
bsb.1:5: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
bsb.1:6: There came a man who was sent from God. His name was John.
bsb.1:7: He came as a witness to testify about the Light, so that through him everyone might believe.
bsb.1:8: He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light.
bsb.1:9: The true Light who gives light to every man was coming into the world.
bsb.1:10: He was in the world, and though the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him.
bsb.1:11: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.
bsb.1:12: But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God—
bsb.1:13: children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God.
bsb.1:14: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
bsb.1:15: John testified concerning Him. He cried out, saying, “This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’”
bsb.1:16: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
bsb.1:17: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
bsb.1:18: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.
bsb.1:19: And this was John’s testimony when the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, “Who are you?”
bsb.1:20: He did not refuse to confess, but openly declared, “I am not the Christ.”
bsb.1:21: “Then who are you?” they inquired. “Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
bsb.1:22: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
bsb.1:23: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’”
bsb.1:24: Then the Pharisees who had been sent
bsb.1:25: asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
bsb.1:26: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.
bsb.1:27: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”
bsb.1:28: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
bsb.1:29: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
bsb.1:30: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’
bsb.1:31: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”
bsb.1:32: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.
bsb.1:33: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
bsb.1:34: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.”
bsb.1:35: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
bsb.1:36: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
bsb.1:37: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.
bsb.1:38: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”
bsb.1:39: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.
bsb.1:40: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.
bsb.1:41: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
bsb.1:42: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter).
bsb.1:43: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”
bsb.1:44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
bsb.1:45: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold—Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
bsb.1:46: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.
bsb.1:47: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”
bsb.1:48: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
bsb.1:49: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
bsb.1:50: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
bsb.1:51: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
bsb.2:1: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,
bsb.2:2: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
bsb.2:3: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”
bsb.2:4: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”
bsb.2:5: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”
bsb.2:6: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.
bsb.2:7: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.
bsb.2:8: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so,
bsb.2:9: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside
bsb.2:10: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”
bsb.2:11: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
bsb.2:12: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
bsb.2:13: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
bsb.2:14: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.
bsb.2:15: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.
bsb.2:16: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”
bsb.2:17: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”
bsb.2:18: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”
bsb.2:19: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”
bsb.2:20: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”
bsb.2:21: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.
bsb.2:22: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
bsb.2:23: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.
bsb.2:24: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.
bsb.2:25: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.
bsb.3:1: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
bsb.3:2: He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.”
bsb.3:3: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.”
bsb.3:4: “How can a man be born when he is old?” Nicodemus asked. “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?”
bsb.3:5: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.
bsb.3:6: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.
bsb.3:7: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’
bsb.3:8: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”
bsb.3:10: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?
bsb.3:11: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.
bsb.3:12: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
bsb.3:13: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of Man.
bsb.3:14: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
bsb.3:15: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
bsb.3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.
bsb.3:17: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.
bsb.3:18: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.
bsb.3:19: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.
bsb.3:20: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.
bsb.3:21: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.”
bsb.3:22: After this, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized.
bsb.3:23: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because the water was plentiful there, and people kept coming to be baptized.
bsb.3:24: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)
bsb.3:25: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing.
bsb.3:26: So John’s disciples came to him and said, “Look, Rabbi, the One who was with you beyond the Jordan, the One you testified about—He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him.”
bsb.3:27: John replied, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.
bsb.3:28: You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’
bsb.3:29: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom’s voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.
bsb.3:30: He must increase; I must decrease.
bsb.3:31: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
bsb.3:32: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.
bsb.3:33: Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.
bsb.3:34: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.
bsb.3:35: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.
bsb.3:36: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.”
bsb.4:1: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John
bsb.4:2: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),
bsb.4:3: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.
bsb.4:4: Now He had to pass through Samaria.
bsb.4:5: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
bsb.4:6: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
bsb.4:7: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
bsb.4:8: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)
bsb.4:9: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)
bsb.4:10: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
bsb.4:11: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?
bsb.4:12: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”
bsb.4:13: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
bsb.4:14: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”
bsb.4:15: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”
bsb.4:16: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”
bsb.4:17: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.
bsb.4:18: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”
bsb.4:19: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.
bsb.4:20: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”
bsb.4:21: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
bsb.4:22: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.
bsb.4:23: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
bsb.4:24: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
bsb.4:25: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”
bsb.4:26: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.”
bsb.4:27: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”
bsb.4:28: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,
bsb.4:29: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”
bsb.4:30: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.
bsb.4:31: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”
bsb.4:32: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”
bsb.4:33: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”
bsb.4:34: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.
bsb.4:35: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.
bsb.4:36: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
bsb.4:37: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.
bsb.4:38: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.”
bsb.4:39: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”
bsb.4:40: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.
bsb.4:41: And many more believed because of His message.
bsb.4:42: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.”
bsb.4:43: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
bsb.4:44: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
bsb.4:45: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.
bsb.4:46: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.
bsb.4:47: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.
bsb.4:48: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”
bsb.4:49: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”
bsb.4:50: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.
bsb.4:51: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.
bsb.4:52: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour.”
bsb.4:53: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.
bsb.4:54: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.
bsb.5:1: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
bsb.5:2: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
bsb.5:3: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.
bsb.5:5: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
bsb.5:6: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”
bsb.5:7: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”
bsb.5:8: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”
bsb.5:9: Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk. Now this happened on the Sabbath day,
bsb.5:10: so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.”
bsb.5:11: But he answered, “The man who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
bsb.5:12: “Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?” they asked.
bsb.5:13: But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.
bsb.5:14: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”
bsb.5:15: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
bsb.5:16: Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.
bsb.5:17: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”
bsb.5:18: Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
bsb.5:19: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.
bsb.5:20: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.
bsb.5:21: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.
bsb.5:22: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,
bsb.5:23: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
bsb.5:24: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
bsb.5:25: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
bsb.5:26: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.
bsb.5:27: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
bsb.5:28: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice
bsb.5:29: and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
bsb.5:30: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
bsb.5:31: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.
bsb.5:32: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.
bsb.5:33: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
bsb.5:34: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.
bsb.5:35: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.
bsb.5:36: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish—the very works I am doing—testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.
bsb.5:37: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,
bsb.5:38: nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent.
bsb.5:39: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,
bsb.5:40: yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.
bsb.5:41: I do not accept glory from men,
bsb.5:42: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.
bsb.5:43: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.
bsb.5:44: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
bsb.5:45: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
bsb.5:46: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
bsb.5:47: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”
bsb.6:1: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee (that is, the Sea of Tiberias).
bsb.6:2: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.
bsb.6:3: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.
bsb.6:4: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.
bsb.6:5: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”
bsb.6:6: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.
bsb.6:7: Philip answered, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”
bsb.6:8: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,
bsb.6:9: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”
bsb.6:10: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
bsb.6:11: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.
bsb.6:12: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”
bsb.6:13: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
bsb.6:14: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
bsb.6:15: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself.
bsb.6:16: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,
bsb.6:17: got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.
bsb.6:18: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.
bsb.6:19: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea—and they were terrified.
bsb.6:20: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
bsb.6:21: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.
bsb.6:22: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.
bsb.6:23: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
bsb.6:24: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
bsb.6:25: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”
bsb.6:26: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
bsb.6:27: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”
bsb.6:28: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”
bsb.6:29: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”
bsb.6:30: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?
bsb.6:31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
bsb.6:32: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
bsb.6:33: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
bsb.6:34: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”
bsb.6:35: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.
bsb.6:36: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.
bsb.6:37: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.
bsb.6:38: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.
bsb.6:39: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.
bsb.6:40: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”
bsb.6:41: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
bsb.6:42: They were asking, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven?’”
bsb.6:44: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.
bsb.6:45: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me—
bsb.6:46: not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.
bsb.6:47: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.
bsb.6:48: I am the bread of life.
bsb.6:49: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.
bsb.6:50: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
bsb.6:51: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”
bsb.6:52: At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”
bsb.6:53: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.
bsb.6:54: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
bsb.6:55: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
bsb.6:56: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
bsb.6:57: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
bsb.6:58: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.”
bsb.6:59: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
bsb.6:60: On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”
bsb.6:61: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you?
bsb.6:62: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?
bsb.6:63: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
bsb.6:64: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)
bsb.6:65: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”
bsb.6:66: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
bsb.6:67: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”
bsb.6:68: Simon Peter replied, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
bsb.6:69: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.”
bsb.6:70: Jesus answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”
bsb.6:71: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
bsb.7:1: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him.
bsb.7:2: However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.
bsb.7:3: So Jesus’ brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.
bsb.7:4: For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.”
bsb.7:5: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
bsb.7:6: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.
bsb.7:7: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.
bsb.7:8: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”
bsb.7:9: Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
bsb.7:10: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went—not publicly, but in secret.
bsb.7:11: So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, “Where is He?”
bsb.7:12: Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, “He is a good man.” But others replied, “No, He deceives the people.”
bsb.7:13: Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.
bsb.7:14: About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
bsb.7:15: The Jews were amazed and asked, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?”
bsb.7:16: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “It comes from Him who sent Me.
bsb.7:17: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.
bsb.7:18: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.
bsb.7:19: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”
bsb.7:20: “You have a demon,” the crowd replied. “Who is trying to kill You?”
bsb.7:21: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
bsb.7:22: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)
bsb.7:23: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?
bsb.7:24: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.”
bsb.7:25: Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, “Isn’t this the man they are trying to kill?
bsb.7:26: Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?
bsb.7:27: But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”
bsb.7:28: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,
bsb.7:29: but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”
bsb.7:30: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
bsb.7:31: Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?”
bsb.7:32: When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.
bsb.7:33: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
bsb.7:34: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”
bsb.7:35: At this, the Jews said to one another, “Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
bsb.7:36: What does He mean by saying, ‘You will look for Me, but you will not find Me,’ and, ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?”
bsb.7:37: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
bsb.7:38: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”
bsb.7:39: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
bsb.7:40: On hearing these words, some of the people said, “This is truly the Prophet.”
bsb.7:41: Others declared, “This is the Christ.” But still others asked, “How can the Christ come from Galilee?
bsb.7:42: Doesn’t the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived?”
bsb.7:43: So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.
bsb.7:44: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.
bsb.7:45: Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”
bsb.7:46: “Never has anyone spoken like this man!” the officers answered.
bsb.7:47: “Have you also been deceived?” replied the Pharisees.
bsb.7:48: “Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?
bsb.7:49: But this crowd that does not know the law, they are under a curse.”
bsb.7:50: Nicodemus, who had gone to Jesus earlier and who himself was one of them, asked,
bsb.7:51: “Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?”
bsb.7:52: “Aren’t you also from Galilee?” they replied. “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.”
bsb.7:53: Then each went to his own home.
bsb.8:1: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
bsb.8:2: Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
bsb.8:3: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them
bsb.8:4: and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
bsb.8:5: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”
bsb.8:6: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
bsb.8:7: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”
bsb.8:8: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
bsb.8:9: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
bsb.8:10: Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?”
bsb.8:11: “No one, Lord,” she answered. “Then neither do I condemn you,” Jesus declared. “Now go and sin no more.”
bsb.8:12: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
bsb.8:13: So the Pharisees said to Him, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.”
bsb.8:14: Jesus replied, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
bsb.8:15: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
bsb.8:16: But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
bsb.8:17: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
bsb.8:18: I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”
bsb.8:19: “Where is Your Father?” they asked Him. “You do not know Me or My Father,” Jesus answered. “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.”
bsb.8:20: He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
bsb.8:21: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
bsb.8:22: So the Jews began to ask, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
bsb.8:23: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
bsb.8:24: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”
bsb.8:25: “Who are You?” they asked. “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning,” Jesus replied.
bsb.8:26: “I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.”
bsb.8:27: They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
bsb.8:28: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
bsb.8:29: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.”
bsb.8:30: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
bsb.8:31: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
bsb.8:32: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
bsb.8:33: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”
bsb.8:34: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
bsb.8:35: A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son belongs to it forever.
bsb.8:36: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
bsb.8:37: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
bsb.8:38: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
bsb.8:39: “Abraham is our father,” they replied. “If you were children of Abraham,” said Jesus, “you would do the works of Abraham.
bsb.8:40: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
bsb.8:41: You are doing the works of your father.” “We are not illegitimate children,” they declared. “Our only Father is God Himself.”
bsb.8:42: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
bsb.8:43: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.
bsb.8:44: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
bsb.8:45: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
bsb.8:46: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
bsb.8:47: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.”
bsb.8:48: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”
bsb.8:49: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
bsb.8:50: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
bsb.8:51: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”
bsb.8:52: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
bsb.8:53: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”
bsb.8:54: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say ‘He is our God.’
bsb.8:55: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
bsb.8:56: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”
bsb.8:57: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”
bsb.8:58: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am!”
bsb.8:59: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
bsb.9:1: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,
bsb.9:2: and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
bsb.9:3: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.
bsb.9:4: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
bsb.9:5: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
bsb.9:6: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.
bsb.9:7: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.
bsb.9:8: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
bsb.9:9: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.” But the man kept saying, “I am the one.”
bsb.9:10: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.
bsb.9:11: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”
bsb.9:12: “Where is He?” they asked. “I do not know,” he answered.
bsb.9:13: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
bsb.9:14: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
bsb.9:15: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. The man answered, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.”
bsb.9:16: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” And there was division among them.
bsb.9:17: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?” “He is a prophet,” the man replied.
bsb.9:18: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents
bsb.9:19: and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”
bsb.9:20: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.
bsb.9:21: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”
bsb.9:22: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
bsb.9:23: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”
bsb.9:24: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”
bsb.9:25: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”
bsb.9:26: “What did He do to you?” they asked. “How did He open your eyes?”
bsb.9:27: He replied, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”
bsb.9:28: Then they heaped insults on him and said, “You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.
bsb.9:29: We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”
bsb.9:30: “That is remarkable indeed!” the man said. “You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
bsb.9:31: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
bsb.9:32: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.
bsb.9:33: If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.”
bsb.9:34: They replied, “You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us?” And they threw him out.
bsb.9:35: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
bsb.9:36: “Who is He, Sir?” he replied. “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”
bsb.9:37: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”
bsb.9:38: “Lord, I believe,” he said. And he worshiped Jesus.
bsb.9:39: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”
bsb.9:40: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, “Are we blind too?”
bsb.9:41: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”
bsb.10:1: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
bsb.10:2: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
bsb.10:3: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
bsb.10:4: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
bsb.10:5: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”
bsb.10:6: Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.
bsb.10:7: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.
bsb.10:8: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
bsb.10:9: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
bsb.10:10: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
bsb.10:11: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
bsb.10:12: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.
bsb.10:13: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.
bsb.10:14: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,
bsb.10:15: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.
bsb.10:16: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
bsb.10:17: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.
bsb.10:18: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”
bsb.10:19: Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus’ message.
bsb.10:20: Many of them said, “He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?”
bsb.10:21: But others replied, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
bsb.10:22: At that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter,
bsb.10:23: and Jesus was walking in the temple courts in Solomon’s Colonnade.
bsb.10:24: So the Jews gathered around Him and demanded, “How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
bsb.10:25: “I already told you,” Jesus replied, “but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.
bsb.10:26: But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.
bsb.10:27: My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.
bsb.10:28: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
bsb.10:29: My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father’s hand.
bsb.10:30: I and the Father are one.”
bsb.10:31: At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.
bsb.10:32: But Jesus responded, “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?”
bsb.10:33: “We are not stoning You for any good work,” said the Jews, “but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, declare Yourself to be God.”
bsb.10:34: Jesus replied, “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I have said you are gods’?
bsb.10:35: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came—and the Scripture cannot be broken—
