bsb.10:36: then what about the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?
bsb.10:37: If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.
bsb.10:38: But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.”
bsb.10:39: At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp.
bsb.10:40: Then Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stayed there.
bsb.10:41: Many came to Him and said, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.”
bsb.10:42: And many in that place believed in Jesus.
bsb.11:1: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
bsb.11:2: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)
bsb.11:3: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”
bsb.11:4: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
bsb.11:5: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
bsb.11:6: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,
bsb.11:7: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”
bsb.11:8: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”
bsb.11:9: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.
bsb.11:10: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”
bsb.11:11: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
bsb.11:12: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”
bsb.11:13: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.
bsb.11:14: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,
bsb.11:15: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”
bsb.11:16: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”
bsb.11:17: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.
bsb.11:18: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away,
bsb.11:19: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.
bsb.11:20: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him; but Mary stayed at home.
bsb.11:21: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
bsb.11:22: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”
bsb.11:23: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.
bsb.11:24: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
bsb.11:25: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.
bsb.11:26: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”
bsb.11:27: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”
bsb.11:28: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”
bsb.11:29: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.
bsb.11:30: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
bsb.11:31: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.
bsb.11:32: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
bsb.11:33: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.
bsb.11:34: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.
bsb.11:36: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
bsb.11:37: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”
bsb.11:38: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.
bsb.11:39: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”
bsb.11:40: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”
bsb.11:41: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
bsb.11:42: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”
bsb.11:43: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
bsb.11:44: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them.
bsb.11:45: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.
bsb.11:46: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
bsb.11:47: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.
bsb.11:48: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
bsb.11:49: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!
bsb.11:50: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”
bsb.11:51: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,
bsb.11:52: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.
bsb.11:53: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.
bsb.11:54: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.
bsb.11:55: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.
bsb.11:56: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”
bsb.11:57: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.
bsb.12:1: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
bsb.12:2: So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.
bsb.12:3: Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
bsb.12:4: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked,
bsb.12:5: “Why wasn’t this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”
bsb.12:6: Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.
bsb.12:7: “Leave her alone,” Jesus replied. “She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.
bsb.12:8: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.”
bsb.12:9: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
bsb.12:10: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
bsb.12:11: for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus.
bsb.12:12: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
bsb.12:13: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
bsb.12:14: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:
bsb.12:15: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”
bsb.12:16: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
bsb.12:17: Meanwhile, many people continued to testify that they had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.
bsb.12:18: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
bsb.12:19: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!”
bsb.12:20: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
bsb.12:21: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
bsb.12:22: Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.
bsb.12:23: But Jesus replied, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
bsb.12:24: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
bsb.12:25: Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
bsb.12:26: If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
bsb.12:27: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.
bsb.12:28: Father, glorify Your name!” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
bsb.12:29: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.
bsb.12:30: In response, Jesus said, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.
bsb.12:31: Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
bsb.12:32: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.”
bsb.12:33: He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
bsb.12:34: The crowd replied, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
bsb.12:35: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
bsb.12:36: While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.
bsb.12:37: Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.
bsb.12:38: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
bsb.12:39: For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says:
bsb.12:40: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.”
bsb.12:41: Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.
bsb.12:42: Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.
bsb.12:43: For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.
bsb.12:44: Then Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.
bsb.12:45: And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
bsb.12:46: I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.
bsb.12:47: As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
bsb.12:48: There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
bsb.12:49: I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.
bsb.12:50: And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.”
bsb.13:1: It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew that His hour had come to leave this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
bsb.13:2: The evening meal was underway, and the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.
bsb.13:3: Jesus knew that the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
bsb.13:4: So He got up from the supper, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
bsb.13:5: After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him.
bsb.13:6: He came to Simon Peter, who asked Him, “Lord, are You going to wash my feet?”
bsb.13:7: Jesus replied, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.”
bsb.13:8: “Never shall You wash my feet!” Peter told Him. Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.”
bsb.13:9: “Then, Lord,” Simon Peter replied, “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!”
bsb.13:10: Jesus told him, “Whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean. And you are clean, though not all of you.”
bsb.13:11: For He knew who would betray Him. That is why He said, “Not all of you are clean.”
bsb.13:12: When Jesus had washed their feet and put on His outer garments, He reclined with them again and asked, “Do you know what I have done for you?
bsb.13:13: You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am.
bsb.13:14: So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet.
bsb.13:15: I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
bsb.13:16: Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
bsb.13:17: If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.
bsb.13:18: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is to fulfill the Scripture: ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’
bsb.13:19: I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He.
bsb.13:20: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
bsb.13:21: After Jesus had said this, He became troubled in spirit and testified, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
bsb.13:22: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant.
bsb.13:23: One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side.
bsb.13:24: So Simon Peter motioned to him to ask Jesus which one He was talking about.
bsb.13:25: Leaning back against Jesus, he asked, “Lord, who is it?”
bsb.13:26: Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it.” Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
bsb.13:27: And when Judas had taken the morsel, Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to Judas, “What you are about to do, do quickly.”
bsb.13:28: But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him.
bsb.13:29: Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
bsb.13:30: As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night.
bsb.13:31: When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
bsb.13:32: If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself—and will glorify Him at once.
bsb.13:33: Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for Me, and as I said to the Jews, so now I say to you: ‘Where I am going, you cannot come.’
bsb.13:34: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
bsb.13:35: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.”
bsb.13:36: “Lord, where are You going?” Simon Peter asked. Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later.”
bsb.13:37: “Lord,” said Peter, “why can’t I follow You now? I will lay down my life for You.”
bsb.13:38: “Will you lay down your life for Me?” Jesus replied. “Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.
bsb.14:1: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well.
bsb.14:2: In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
bsb.14:3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
bsb.14:4: You know the way to the place where I am going.”
bsb.14:5: “Lord,” said Thomas, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?”
bsb.14:6: Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
bsb.14:7: If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him.”
bsb.14:8: Philip said to Him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
bsb.14:9: Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
bsb.14:10: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.
bsb.14:11: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me—or at least believe on account of the works themselves.
bsb.14:12: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
bsb.14:13: And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
bsb.14:14: If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.
bsb.14:15: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
bsb.14:16: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever—
bsb.14:17: the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.
bsb.14:18: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
bsb.14:19: In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
bsb.14:20: On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
bsb.14:21: Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
bsb.14:22: Judas (not Iscariot) asked Him, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?”
bsb.14:23: Jesus replied, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
bsb.14:24: Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.
bsb.14:25: All this I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
bsb.14:26: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.
bsb.14:27: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.
bsb.14:28: You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
bsb.14:29: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
bsb.14:30: I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me.
bsb.14:31: But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father. Get up! Let us go on from here.
bsb.15:1: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
bsb.15:2: He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
bsb.15:3: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
bsb.15:4: Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.
bsb.15:5: I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.
bsb.15:6: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
bsb.15:7: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
bsb.15:8: This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.
bsb.15:9: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
bsb.15:10: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
bsb.15:11: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
bsb.15:12: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
bsb.15:13: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
bsb.15:14: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
bsb.15:15: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
bsb.15:16: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
bsb.15:17: This is My command to you: Love one another.
bsb.15:18: If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.
bsb.15:19: If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.
bsb.15:20: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘No servant is greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
bsb.15:21: But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.
bsb.15:22: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.
bsb.15:23: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
bsb.15:24: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.
bsb.15:25: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without reason.’
bsb.15:26: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.
bsb.15:27: And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.
bsb.16:1: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
bsb.16:2: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
bsb.16:3: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.
bsb.16:4: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
bsb.16:5: Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’
bsb.16:6: Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.
bsb.16:7: But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
bsb.16:8: And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment:
bsb.16:9: in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me;
bsb.16:10: in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me;
bsb.16:11: and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.
bsb.16:12: I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.
bsb.16:13: However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.
bsb.16:14: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.
bsb.16:15: Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.
bsb.16:16: In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me.”
bsb.16:17: Then some of His disciples asked one another, “Why is He telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’ and ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
bsb.16:18: They kept asking, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’? We do not understand what He is saying.”
bsb.16:19: Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, “Are you asking one another why I said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’?
bsb.16:20: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
bsb.16:21: A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
bsb.16:22: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
bsb.16:23: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
bsb.16:24: Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
bsb.16:25: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
bsb.16:26: In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
bsb.16:27: For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.
bsb.16:28: I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.”
bsb.16:29: His disciples said, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.
bsb.16:30: Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.”
bsb.16:32: “Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
bsb.16:33: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!”
bsb.17:1: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.
bsb.17:2: For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.
bsb.17:3: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
bsb.17:4: I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.
bsb.17:5: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.
bsb.17:6: I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
bsb.17:7: Now they know that everything You have given Me comes from You.
bsb.17:8: For I have given them the words You gave Me, and they have received them. They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
bsb.17:9: I ask on their behalf. I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.
bsb.17:10: All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine; and in them I have been glorified.
bsb.17:11: I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.
bsb.17:12: While I was with them, I protected and preserved them by Your name, the name You gave Me. Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.
bsb.17:13: But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.
bsb.17:14: I have given them Your word and the world has hated them; for they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
bsb.17:15: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
bsb.17:16: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
bsb.17:17: Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.
bsb.17:18: As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.
bsb.17:19: For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth.
bsb.17:20: I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message,
bsb.17:21: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
bsb.17:22: I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one—
bsb.17:23: I in them and You in Me—that they may be perfectly united, so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.
bsb.17:24: Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
bsb.17:25: Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me.
bsb.17:26: And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.”
bsb.18:1: After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.
bsb.18:2: Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.
bsb.18:3: So Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
bsb.18:4: Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you seeking?”
bsb.18:5: “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. Jesus said, “I am He.” And Judas His betrayer was standing there with them.
bsb.18:6: When Jesus said, “I am He,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
bsb.18:7: So He asked them again, “Whom are you seeking?” “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered.
bsb.18:8: “I told you that I am He,” Jesus replied. “So if you are looking for Me, let these men go.”
bsb.18:9: This was to fulfill the word He had spoken: “I have not lost one of those You have given Me.”
bsb.18:10: Then Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
bsb.18:11: “Put your sword back in its sheath!” Jesus said to Peter. “Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?”
bsb.18:12: Then the band of soldiers, with its commander and the officers of the Jews, arrested Jesus and bound Him.
bsb.18:13: They brought Him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
bsb.18:14: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better if one man died for the people.
bsb.18:15: Now Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he also went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
bsb.18:16: But Peter stood outside at the door. Then the disciple who was known to the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
bsb.18:17: At this, the servant girl watching the door said to Peter, “Aren’t you also one of this man’s disciples?” “I am not,” he answered.
bsb.18:18: Because it was cold, the servants and officers were standing around a charcoal fire they had made to keep warm. And Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
bsb.18:19: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
bsb.18:20: “I have spoken openly to the world,” Jesus answered. “I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
bsb.18:21: Why are you asking Me? Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.”
bsb.18:22: When Jesus had said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped Him in the face and said, “Is this how You answer the high priest?”
bsb.18:23: Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?”
bsb.18:24: Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
bsb.18:25: Simon Peter was still standing and warming himself. So they asked him, “Aren’t you also one of His disciples?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
bsb.18:26: One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, asked, “Didn’t I see you with Him in the garden?”
bsb.18:27: Peter denied it once more, and immediately a rooster crowed.
bsb.18:28: Then they led Jesus away from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. By now it was early morning, and the Jews did not enter the Praetorium, to avoid being defiled and unable to eat the Passover.
bsb.18:29: So Pilate went out to them and asked, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
bsb.18:30: “If He were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed Him over to you.”
bsb.18:31: “You take Him and judge Him by your own law,” Pilate told them. “We are not permitted to execute anyone,” the Jews replied.
bsb.18:32: This was to fulfill the word that Jesus had spoken to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
bsb.18:33: Pilate went back into the Praetorium, summoned Jesus, and asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
bsb.18:34: “Are you saying this on your own,” Jesus asked, “or did others tell you about Me?”
bsb.18:35: “Am I a Jew?” Pilate replied. “Your own people and chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?”
bsb.18:36: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My kingdom is not of this realm.”
bsb.18:37: “Then You are a king!” Pilate said. “You say that I am a king,” Jesus answered. “For this reason I was born and have come into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice.”
bsb.18:38: “What is truth?” Pilate asked. And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and told them, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.
bsb.18:39: But it is your custom that I release to you one prisoner at the Passover. So then, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
bsb.18:40: “Not this man,” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” (Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist.)
bsb.19:1: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.
bsb.19:2: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.
bsb.19:3: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.
bsb.19:4: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
bsb.19:5: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
bsb.19:6: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” “You take Him and crucify Him,” Pilate replied, “for I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
bsb.19:7: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”
bsb.19:8: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,
bsb.19:9: and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.
bsb.19:10: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”
bsb.19:11: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”
bsb.19:12: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
bsb.19:13: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
bsb.19:14: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”
bsb.19:15: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!” “Shall I crucify your King?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” replied the chief priests.
bsb.19:16: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.
bsb.19:17: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
bsb.19:18: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
bsb.19:19: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
bsb.19:20: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
bsb.19:21: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”
bsb.19:22: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
bsb.19:23: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
bsb.19:24: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” So that is what the soldiers did.
bsb.19:25: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.
bsb.19:26: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
bsb.19:27: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home.
bsb.19:28: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
bsb.19:29: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.
bsb.19:30: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
bsb.19:31: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.
bsb.19:32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.
bsb.19:33: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
bsb.19:34: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.
bsb.19:35: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
bsb.19:36: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
bsb.19:37: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”
bsb.19:38: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.
bsb.19:39: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.
bsb.19:40: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.
bsb.19:41: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
bsb.19:42: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.
bsb.20:1: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.
bsb.20:2: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”
bsb.20:3: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
bsb.20:4: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
bsb.20:5: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
bsb.20:6: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
bsb.20:7: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.
bsb.20:8: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
bsb.20:9: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
bsb.20:10: Then the disciples returned to their homes.
bsb.20:11: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,
bsb.20:12: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
bsb.20:13: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked. “Because they have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”
bsb.20:14: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not recognize that it was Jesus.
bsb.20:15: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”
bsb.20:16: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to Him in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”).
bsb.20:17: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
bsb.20:18: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them what He had said to her.
bsb.20:19: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.
bsb.20:20: After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
bsb.20:21: Again Jesus said to them, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.”
bsb.20:22: When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
bsb.20:23: If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.”
bsb.20:24: Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.
bsb.20:25: So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.”
bsb.20:26: Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
bsb.20:27: Then Jesus said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.”
bsb.20:28: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”
bsb.20:29: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
bsb.20:30: Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
bsb.20:31: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
bsb.21:1: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way:
bsb.21:2: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
bsb.21:3: Simon Peter told them, “I am going fishing.” “We will go with you,” they said. So they went out and got into the boat, but caught nothing that night.
bsb.21:4: Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
bsb.21:5: So He called out to them, “Children, do you have any fish?” “No,” they answered.
bsb.21:6: He told them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
bsb.21:7: Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he had removed it) and jumped into the sea.
bsb.21:8: The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.
bsb.21:9: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
bsb.21:10: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
bsb.21:11: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
bsb.21:12: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
bsb.21:13: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
bsb.21:14: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.
bsb.21:15: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”
bsb.21:16: Jesus asked a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus told him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
bsb.21:17: Jesus asked a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?” “Lord, You know all things,” he replied. “You know I love You.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.
bsb.21:18: Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.”
bsb.21:19: Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. And after He had said this, He told him, “Follow Me.”
bsb.21:20: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. He was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper to ask, “Lord, who is going to betray You?”
bsb.21:21: When Peter saw him, he asked, “Lord, what about him?”
bsb.21:22: Jesus answered, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you? You follow Me!”
bsb.21:23: Because of this, the rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. However, Jesus did not say that he would not die, but only, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you?”
bsb.21:24: This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down. And we know that his testimony is true.
bsb.21:25: There are many more things that Jesus did. If all of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written.

asv.1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
asv.1:2: The same was in the beginning with God.
asv.1:3: All things were made through him; and without him was not anything made that hath been made.
asv.1:4: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
asv.1:5: And the light shineth in the darkness; and the darkness apprehended it not.
asv.1:6: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.
asv.1:7: The same came for witness, that he might bear witness of the light, that all might believe through him.
asv.1:8: He was not the light, but came that he might bear witness of the light.
asv.1:9: There was the true light, even the light which lighteth every man, coming into the world.
asv.1:10: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world knew him not.
asv.1:11: He came unto his own, and they that were his own received him not.
asv.1:12: But as many as received him, to them gave he the right to become children of God, even to them that believe on his name:
asv.1:13: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
asv.1:14: And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth.
asv.1:15: John beareth witness of him, and crieth, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that cometh after me is become before me: for he was before me.
asv.1:16: For of his fulness we all received, and grace for grace.
asv.1:17: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
asv.1:18: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
asv.1:19: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent unto him from Jerusalem priests and Levites to ask him, Who art thou?
asv.1:20: And he confessed, and denied not; and he confessed, I am not the Christ.
asv.1:21: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elijah? And he saith, I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered, No.
asv.1:22: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?
asv.1:23: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.
asv.1:24: And they had been sent from the Pharisees.
asv.1:25: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why then baptizest thou, if thou art not the Christ, neither Elijah, neither the prophet?
asv.1:26: John answered them, saying, I baptize in water: in the midst of you standeth one whom ye know not,
asv.1:27: even he that cometh after me, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to unloose.
asv.1:28: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
asv.1:29: On the morrow he seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sin of the world!
asv.1:30: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man who is become before me: for he was before me.
asv.1:31: And I knew him not; but that he should be made manifest to Israel, for this cause came I baptizing in water.
asv.1:32: And John bare witness, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven; and it abode upon him.
asv.1:33: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize in water, he said unto me, Upon whomsoever thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and abiding upon him, the same is he that baptizeth in the Holy Spirit.
asv.1:34: And I have seen, and have borne witness that this is the Son of God.
asv.1:35: Again on the morrow John was standing, and two of his disciples;
asv.1:36: and he looked upon Jesus as he walked, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God!
asv.1:37: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
asv.1:38: And Jesus turned, and beheld them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? And they said unto him, Rabbi (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), where abidest thou?
asv.1:39: He saith unto them, Come, and ye shall see. They came therefore and saw where he abode; and they abode with him that day: it was about the tenth hour.
asv.1:40: One of the two that heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
asv.1:41: He findeth first his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah (which is, being interpreted, Christ).
asv.1:42: He brought him unto Jesus. Jesus looked upon him, and said, Thou art Simon the son of John: thou shalt be called Cephas (which is by interpretation, Peter).
asv.1:43: On the morrow he was minded to go forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philip: and Jesus saith unto him, Follow me.
asv.1:44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.
asv.1:45: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
asv.1:46: And Nathanael said unto him, Can any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.
asv.1:47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
asv.1:48: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
asv.1:49: Nathanael answered him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art King of Israel.
asv.1:50: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee underneath the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.
asv.1:51: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
asv.2:1: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
asv.2:2: and Jesus also was bidden, and his disciples, to the marriage.
asv.2:3: And when the wine failed, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.
asv.2:4: And Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.
asv.2:5: His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
asv.2:6: Now there were six waterpots of stone set there after the Jews’ manner of purifying, containing two or three firkins apiece.
asv.2:7: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
asv.2:8: And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the ruler of the feast. And they bare it.
asv.2:9: And when the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and knew not whence it was (but the servants that had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast calleth the bridegroom,
asv.2:10: and saith unto him, Every man setteth on first the good wine; and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse: thou hast kept the good wine until now.
asv.2:11: This beginning of his signs did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory; and his disciples believed on him.
asv.2:12: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples; and there they abode not many days.
asv.2:13: And the passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
asv.2:14: And he found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
asv.2:15: and he made a scourge of cords, and cast all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew their tables;
asv.2:16: and to them that sold the doves he said, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house a house of merchandise.
asv.2:17: His disciples remembered that it was written, Zeal for thy house shall eat me up.
asv.2:18: The Jews therefore answered and said unto him, What sign showest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?
asv.2:19: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
asv.2:20: The Jews therefore said, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou raise it up in three days?
asv.2:21: But he spake of the temple of his body.
asv.2:22: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he spake this; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.
asv.2:23: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, during the feast, many believed on his name, beholding his signs which he did.
asv.2:24: But Jesus did not trust himself unto them, for that he knew all men,
asv.2:25: and because he needed not that any one should bear witness concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.
asv.3:1: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:
asv.3:2: the same came unto him by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God; for no one can do these signs that thou doest, except God be with him.
asv.3:3: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
asv.3:4: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?
asv.3:5: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
asv.3:6: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
asv.3:7: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born anew.
asv.3:8: The wind bloweth where it will, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
asv.3:9: Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?
asv.3:10: Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou the teacher of Israel, and understandest not these things?
asv.3:11: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that which we know, and bear witness of that which we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.
asv.3:12: If I told you earthly things and ye believe not, how shall ye believe if I tell you heavenly things?
asv.3:13: And no one hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended out of heaven, even the Son of man, who is in heaven.
asv.3:14: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up;
asv.3:15: that whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life.
asv.3:16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on him should not perish, but have eternal life.
asv.3:17: For God sent not the Son into the world to judge the world; but that the world should be saved through him.
asv.3:18: He that believeth on him is not judged: he that believeth not hath been judged already, because he hath not believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God.
asv.3:19: And this is the judgment, that the light is come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.
asv.3:20: For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, and cometh not to the light, lest his works should be reproved.
asv.3:21: But he that doeth the truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest, that they have been wrought in God.
asv.3:22: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judæa; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.
asv.3:23: And John also was baptizing in Ænon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.
asv.3:24: For John was not yet cast into prison.
asv.3:25: There arose therefore a questioning on the part of John’s disciples with a Jew about purifying.
asv.3:26: And they came unto John, and said to him, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond the Jordan, to whom thou hast borne witness, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him.
asv.3:27: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it have been given him from heaven.
asv.3:28: Ye yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but, that I am sent before him.
asv.3:29: He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, that standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice: this my joy therefore is made full.
asv.3:30: He must increase, but I must decrease.
asv.3:31: He that cometh from above is above all: he that is of the earth is of the earth, and of the earth he speaketh: he that cometh from heaven is above all.
asv.3:32: What he hath seen and heard, of that he beareth witness; and no man receiveth his witness.
asv.3:33: He that hath received his witness hath set his seal to this, that God is true.
asv.3:34: For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for he giveth not the Spirit by measure.
asv.3:35: The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.
asv.3:36: He that believeth on the Son hath eternal life; but he that obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.
asv.4:1: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
asv.4:2: (although Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples),
asv.4:3: he left Judæa, and departed again into Galilee.
asv.4:4: And he must needs pass through Samaria.
asv.4:5: So he cometh to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph:
asv.4:6: and Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
asv.4:7: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
asv.4:8: For his disciples were gone away into the city to buy food.
asv.4:9: The Samaritan woman therefore saith unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a Samaritan woman? (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
asv.4:10: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
asv.4:11: The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: whence then hast thou that living water?
asv.4:12: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his sons, and his cattle?
asv.4:13: Jesus answered and said unto her, Every one that drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
asv.4:14: but whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall become in him a well of water springing up unto eternal life.
asv.4:15: The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come all the way hither to draw.
asv.4:16: Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.
asv.4:17: The woman answered and said unto him, I have no husband. Jesus saith unto her, Thou saidst well, I have no husband:
asv.4:18: for thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: this hast thou said truly.
asv.4:19: The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.
asv.4:20: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.
asv.4:21: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, shall ye worship the Father.
asv.4:22: Ye worship that which ye know not: we worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.
asv.4:23: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth: for such doth the Father seek to be his worshippers.
asv.4:24: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
asv.4:25: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messiah cometh (he that is called Christ): when he is come, he will declare unto us all things.
asv.4:26: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.
asv.4:27: And upon this came his disciples; and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why speakest thou with her?
asv.4:28: So the woman left her waterpot, and went away into the city, and saith to the people,
asv.4:29: Come, see a man, who told me all things that ever I did: can this be the Christ?
asv.4:30: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.
asv.4:31: In the mean while the disciples prayed him, saying, Rabbi, eat.
asv.4:32: But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not.
asv.4:33: The disciples therefore said one to another, Hath any man brought him aught to eat?
asv.4:34: Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to accomplish his work.
asv.4:35: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh the harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields, that they are white already unto harvest.
asv.4:36: He that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal; that he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.
asv.4:37: For herein is the saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.
asv.4:38: I sent you to reap that whereon ye have not labored: others have labored, and ye are entered into their labor.
asv.4:39: And from that city many of the Samaritans believed on him because of the word of the woman, who testified, He told me all things that ever I did.
asv.4:40: So when the Samaritans came unto him, they besought him to abide with them: and he abode there two days.
asv.4:41: And many more believed because of his word;
asv.4:42: and they said to the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy speaking: for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world.
asv.4:43: And after the two days he went forth from thence into Galilee.
asv.4:44: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honor in his own country.
asv.4:45: So when he came into Galilee, the Galilæans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.
asv.4:46: He came therefore again unto Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.
asv.4:47: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judæa into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son; for he was at the point of death.
asv.4:48: Jesus therefore said unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will in no wise believe.
asv.4:49: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.
asv.4:50: Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word that Jesus spake unto him, and he went his way.
asv.4:51: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, saying, that his son lived.
asv.4:52: So he inquired of them the hour when he began to amend. They said therefore unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
asv.4:53: So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house.
asv.4:54: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judæa into Galilee.
asv.5:1: After these things there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
asv.5:2: Now there is in Jerusalem by the sheep gate a pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches.
asv.5:3: In these lay a multitude of them that were sick, blind, halt, withered.
asv.5:5: And a certain man was there, who had been thirty and eight years in his infirmity.
asv.5:6: When Jesus saw him lying, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wouldest thou be made whole?
asv.5:7: The sick man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.
asv.5:8: Jesus saith unto him, Arise, take up thy bed, and walk.
asv.5:9: And straightway the man was made whole, and took up his bed and walked. Now it was the sabbath on that day.
asv.5:10: So the Jews said unto him that was cured, It is the sabbath, and it is not lawful for thee to take up thy bed.
asv.5:11: But he answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up thy bed, and walk.
asv.5:12: They asked him, Who is the man that said unto thee, Take up thy bed, and walk?
asv.5:13: But he that was healed knew not who it was; for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in the place.
asv.5:14: Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing befall thee.
asv.5:15: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.
asv.5:16: And for this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the sabbath.
asv.5:17: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh even until now, and I work.
asv.5:18: For this cause therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only brake the sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
asv.5:19: Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doing: for what things soever he doeth, these the Son also doeth in like manner.
asv.5:20: For the Father loveth the Son, and showeth him all things that himself doeth: and greater works than these will he show him, that ye may marvel.
asv.5:21: For as the Father raiseth the dead and giveth them life, even so the Son also giveth life to whom he will.
asv.5:22: For neither doth the Father judge any man, but he hath given all judgment unto the Son;
asv.5:23: that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He that honoreth not the Son honoreth not the Father that sent him.
asv.5:24: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth him that sent me, hath eternal life, and cometh not into judgment, but hath passed out of death into life.
asv.5:25: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour cometh, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live.
asv.5:26: For as the Father hath life in himself, even so gave he to the Son also to have life in himself:
asv.5:27: and he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.
asv.5:28: Marvel not at this: for the hour cometh, in which all that are in the tombs shall hear his voice,
asv.5:29: and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.
asv.5:30: I can of myself do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is righteous; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.
asv.5:31: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
asv.5:32: It is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.
asv.5:33: Ye have sent unto John, and he hath borne witness unto the truth.
asv.5:34: But the witness which I receive is not from man: howbeit I say these things, that ye may be saved.
asv.5:35: He was the lamp that burneth and shineth; and ye were willing to rejoice for a season in his light.
asv.5:36: But the witness which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father hath given me to accomplish, the very works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me.
asv.5:37: And the Father that sent me, he hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.
asv.5:38: And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he sent, him ye believe not.
asv.5:39: Ye search the scriptures, because ye think that in them ye have eternal life; and these are they which bear witness of me;
asv.5:40: and ye will not come to me, that ye may have life.
asv.5:41: I receive not glory from men.
asv.5:42: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in yourselves.
asv.5:43: I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.
asv.5:44: How can ye believe, who receive glory one of another, and the glory that cometh from the only God ye seek not?
asv.5:45: Think not that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, on whom ye have set your hope.
asv.5:46: For if ye believed Moses, ye would believe me; for he wrote of me.
asv.5:47: But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?
asv.6:1: After these things Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is the sea of Tiberias.
asv.6:2: And a great multitude followed him, because they beheld the signs which he did on them that were sick.
asv.6:3: And Jesus went up into the mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.
asv.6:4: Now the passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.
asv.6:5: Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude cometh unto him, saith unto Philip, Whence are we to buy bread, that these may eat?
asv.6:6: And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.
asv.6:7: Philip answered him, Two hundred shillings’ worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one may take a little.
asv.6:8: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, saith unto him,
asv.6:9: There is a lad here, who hath five barley loaves, and two fishes: but what are these among so many?
asv.6:10: Jesus said, Make the people sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
asv.6:11: Jesus therefore took the loaves; and having given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down; likewise also of the fishes as much as they would.
asv.6:12: And when they were filled, he saith unto his disciples, Gather up the broken pieces which remain over, that nothing be lost.
asv.6:13: So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which remained over unto them that had eaten.
asv.6:14: When therefore the people saw the sign which he did, they said, This is of a truth the prophet that cometh into the world.
asv.6:15: Jesus therefore perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force, to make him king, withdrew again into the mountain himself alone.
asv.6:16: And when evening came, his disciples went down unto the sea;
asv.6:17: and they entered into a boat, and were going over the sea unto Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
asv.6:18: And the sea was rising by reason of a great wind that blew.
asv.6:19: When therefore they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they behold Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the boat: and they were afraid.
asv.6:20: But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.
asv.6:21: They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat: and straightway the boat was at the land whither they were going.
asv.6:22: On the morrow the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, save one, and that Jesus entered not with his disciples into the boat, but that his disciples went away alone
asv.6:23: (howbeit there came boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks):
asv.6:24: when the multitude therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they themselves got into the boats, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
asv.6:25: And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
asv.6:26: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw signs, but because ye ate of the loaves, and were filled.
asv.6:27: Work not for the food which perisheth, but for the food which abideth unto eternal life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him the Father, even God, hath sealed.
asv.6:28: They said therefore unto him, What must we do, that we may work the works of God?
asv.6:29: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.
asv.6:30: They said therefore unto him, What then doest thou for a sign, that we may see, and believe thee? what workest thou?
asv.6:31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.
asv.6:32: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread out of heaven.
asv.6:33: For the bread of God is that which cometh down out of heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
asv.6:34: They said therefore unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
asv.6:35: Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
asv.6:36: But I said unto you, that ye have seen me, and yet believe not.
